transcript: [00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood Inference, with Priya our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Marta Chen: Hi all — Marta here, CTO at IonWave. we have Rahul and Sofia as well.
[00:13] Priya Shah: hi! excited to dig into the workload and cost modeling — want to make sure the pilot is scoped to get clear unit economics.

[00:22] Rahul Patel: high level — we're running a chat assistant and a summarization pipeline. average conversation is ~220 tokens out, ~120 tokens in, so roughly 340 tokens per session. Peak is around 120 concurrent sessions, sustained 3k sessions/day. budget for pilot is tight, roughly $15k for the 4 weeks including infra and benchmarking costs.
[00:44] Jordan Kim: great, that's helpful. are you currently running any managed LLMs? like OpenAI or self-hosted?
[00:50] Rahul Patel: we're on OpenAI for dev and some prod, but costs spiked. also testing a local Llama2 quantized variant for on-prem experiments but ops overhead is high.

[00:59] Priya Shah: ok. so for the pilot we'll model both hosted (Redwood API) and Dedicated/Private options. main knobs that change unit economics: batching, cache hit rate, model quantization, and the token distribution (prompt vs generated).
[01:12] Sofia Torres: question — our SLAs require 95th percentile response latency under 600ms for chat flows. is that realistic with batching?

[01:19] Priya Shah: yes but depends on target batch windows and sequence lengths. for low-latency SLOs we recommend dynamic batching with small max batch size and a short max wait (e.g., 5-10ms). caching helps a lot for repeated prefixes — prefix/KV cache can cut generation token counts substantially for reranked or repeated prompts.
[01:38] Marta Chen: can you give rough per-token numbers? we need to compare to our OpenAI bill.

[01:43] Jordan Kim: rough starting point — for our hosted tier with a mid-sized model (around 13B optimized), we estimate $0.30–$0.80 per 1k tokens depending on batching and cache hit. Dedicated runs and quantized variants can drop that to $0.08–$0.25 per 1k tokens, but add reserved capacity commitments.
[02:01] Rahul Patel: that's a wide range. what's driving the top end?

[02:05] Priya Shah: mainly small batches (latency-driven), low cache hit rates, and larger sequence lengths. also peak tail latency — if you need headroom for spikes we route to more expensive nodes or keep spare capacity which increases unit cost.
[02:18] Sofia Torres: for our workload, we have heavy tail queries but also many repeat prompts (help center style). what cache hit rates should we expect?

[02:26] Priya Shah: with aggressive prefix caching and deduping, a realistic pilot hit rate could be 20–40% depending on prompt variability. for customer knowledge base prompts we've seen 40–60% hits. so we'll model a conservative 25% and an optimistic 45% scenario.

[02:42] Jordan Kim: another lever is quantization — 8-bit or 4-bit quantized runtimes can reduce GPU memory and increase throughput, lowering cost per token; quality regressions are model-dependent. we usually recommend testing 4-bit for non-critical outputs and 8-bit for chat where safety and quality matters.
[02:58] Marta Chen: timeline — what would a pilot look like?

[03:02] Jordan Kim: propose 4 weeks: week 0 onboarding + security review, week 1 data upload + baseline benchmarks, week 2 optimizations (batching, caching, quant), week 3 production-scale bench and SLO validation. deliverables: benchmark report, cost model, and recommended config for production rollout.
[03:20] Rahul Patel: for benchmarks we need the script. can you share a harness that reproduces our traffic shape (burstiness, token distributions)?
[03:26] Priya Shah: yes we'll share a JMeter-style harness and a small infra repo to run against Redwood endpoints. will include param for concurrency, seq lengths, and cache patterns.
[03:35] Marta Chen: security — we need SOC 2, VPC peering, and KMS integration. do you support customer-managed keys and VPC endpoints in the pilot?

[03:43] Jordan Kim: yes. Hosted can run with VPC peering and we integrate with common KMS providers. for stricter needs we can spin up a Private deployment (customer-controlled network) for the pilot — adds setup time but meets the highest bar.
[03:54] Sofia Torres: how much additional time for Private vs Dedicated?
[03:57] Priya Shah: Dedicated can be ready in ~2 weeks with reserved nodes; Private (air-gapped or customer-managed) tends to be 4–6 weeks because of infra access and security validation.
[04:06] Rahul Patel: ok for the pilot we prefer Hosted with VPC peering to move faster, but want a path to Dedicated if economics look good.

[04:13] Jordan Kim: that's a common pattern. for cost modeling we'll produce per-token estimates under several scenarios: hosted baseline, hosted with 25/45% cache, dedicated 1 GPU pool, and dedicated with quantization. we'll also show break-even point vs your current OpenAI spend.

[04:25] Marta Chen: our current spend is roughly $22k/month for prod LLM usage, but quality/latency issues mean we can't scale without cost blowup. pilot budget is $15k and if results look promising we could push to dedicated commit discussions.

[04:36] Priya Shah: great, we'll prioritize keeping pilot within that budget. two immediate questions for modeling: expected average tokens/session (you gave ~340), and target peak QPS or concurrent sessions for pilot. Rahul?
[04:48] Rahul Patel: aim to simulate up to 150 concurrent sessions during peak; daily average concurrency more like 40–60. We'll also send a representative 3-day trace extract.

[04:58] Jordan Kim: perfect. that trace helps produce accurate batching efficiency numbers — batching efficiency is heavily dependent on arrival patterns. with steady arrivals, batching can increase throughput 2–4x; with spiky arrival you get less benefit unless you raise max batch size or use background batching windows.
[05:12] Sofia Torres: is there a simple cost formula we can use to sanity check numbers internally?

[05:16] Priya Shah: yes — start with cost_per_token = (infra_cost_per_minute / tokens_per_minute) + model_software_fee. Redwood typically shows it as: compute_cost_component + platform_fee_component. we'll produce a spreadsheet showing per-1k token cost under different configs.
[05:30] Marta Chen: examples of compute configurations?

[05:32] Priya Shah: e.g., a single A100-equivalent node serving a 13B model with quantization might sustain X tokens/sec (we'll fill numbers once we run bench). Typical pricing bands for Dedicated per-month reserved starts around $8k-$12k per GPU node depending on contract; hosted per-token rates reflect our shared infra and support tiers.
[05:50] Rahul Patel: we care about 95th percentile tail latency. can the bench report include p50/p95/p99 and token throughput?
[05:57] Priya Shah: absolutely — each run will include p50/p95/p99 per-request and per-token as well as end-to-end latency under realistic prompt+generate mixes.
[06:06] Jordan Kim: also we'll include a sensitivity analysis: how costs change with cache hit rate, model size, and batching window. that usually helps procurement see how predictable costs are.
[06:14] Marta Chen: any concerns about hallucination or quality regressions from quantization? we need to maintain our NPS-quality signal.

[06:20] Priya Shah: quality regressions are model and task-specific. our eval framework runs side-by-side comparisons on a labeled prompt set to quantify regression in metrics you care about — we recommend keeping human evaluation for edge cases during pilot.
[06:32] Rahul Patel: what about reranking or hybrid retrieval augmentation? that affects token counts too.

[06:36] Jordan Kim: yes — retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) increases prompt size but often reduces generation length. we should model RAG separately: cost of retrieval (embedding calls) + larger prompt tokens + generation tokens. embeddings costs are usually lower per unit but add to total.
[06:49] Sofia Torres: can you show a worked example in the pilot spreadsheet? like 1k sessions/day with 25% cache vs 45% cache and resulting monthly cost.

[06:56] Priya Shah: yes we'll include sample scenarios and a toggle for number of sessions, avg tokens, cache hit, and batch efficiency. we'll also include a break-even calculation vs your current OpenAI spend.
[07:05] Marta Chen: would you be able to run an initial microbenchmark against a small subset this week just to sanity check numbers?

[07:11] Priya Shah: we can run a microbench within 48 hours if you provide API access or allow Redwood test tokens against a staging endpoint. ideally we run it against your sample traces to mimic arrival patterns.
[07:21] Rahul Patel: we'll provision an API key and upload the trace. note we need masked PII in the sample — can't share customer data.
[07:28] Jordan Kim: totally — we can sign an NDA and you can scrub PII or tokenized it. privacy is standard for pilots.
[07:34] Marta Chen: ok. one more thing — procurement will ask for TCO beyond just tokens: monitoring costs, support, and incident management. can you capture an ops estimate?

[07:42] Jordan Kim: yes we'll include monitoring/observability add-on and an ops support tier estimate. for pilots we often include basic monitoring in the price and provide optional premium retention/alerts for enterprise.
[07:51] Sofia Torres: curious about what metrics you recommend we track to decide success at the end of pilot.

[07:55] Priya Shah: recommended success criteria: 1) functional parity/quality — no significant regression on labeled set; 2) performance — p95 latency under 600ms for chat flows; 3) unit economics — projected cost per 1k tokens meeting target and beating or matching current run-rate; 4) operational readiness — monitoring, rollout plans, and security checklist complete.
[08:14] Rahul Patel: for quality threshold, can you quantify acceptable delta? e.g., less than 2% drop on F1-like metric or NPS?
[08:20] Priya Shah: we usually set an acceptance window: human eval delta <3 points or automated metric drop <2–3% depending on task. we can agree a concrete metric for your prompt set.

[08:30] Jordan Kim: ok to summarize — we'll send a pilot SOW, benchmark harness, and a cost worksheet; IonWave will send sample traces and confirm security requirements. pilot timeline target starts next Monday if we sign SOW — 4 weeks total.
[08:43] Marta Chen: yes that timeline works; procurement will need the SOW for approvals, budgeting, and we'll loop them in once we see numbers.
[08:50] Rahul Patel: one last tech question — how do you calculate cache hit rate for KV cache? is it based on token prefix dedupe or full prompt match?

[08:57] Priya Shah: KV/prefix cache works on repeated prefix tokens and intermediate KV reuse across sessions when prompts/share conversation context. we calculate effective hit as fraction of generation tokens avoided due to cache. we'll instrument that in the bench and report both raw hit rate and effective token savings.

[09:14] Jordan Kim: nothing major. we'll follow up with the SOW and pricing by Monday; Priya will share the bench harness and config options.
